findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the transport-attempt seam's actual application point (the provider transport built from the effective config in anthropic_model.py / bedrock_model.py via cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts), not just the 'native/prompted structured-output paths', so the one-transport-attempt bound is enforced where the retry envelope is constructed.
evidence: anthropic_model.py:113 `attempts = max(1, int(cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts))` then stop_after_attempt(attempts) at :122
Transport retry envelope is built when the Model/provider is constructed inside run() from the effective cfg, not in _pai_structured's native/prompted branches

_effective_config (runner.py:216) currently substitutes only the model, so lowering the transport attempts requires either that function or an explicit provider-transport seam to read a request-local value
findings.finding: The transport-attempt limit is consumed at provider/model construction from cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts (anthropic_model.py:113 / bedrock_model.py:122 tenacity stop_after_attempt), not in the native/prompted structured-output paths the plan enumerates as the application points; the plan's application clause should name the provider-transport builder (reached via the effective config) so the edit set for the transport seam is complete.
findings.location: Repair plan, bullet 2 ('Apply those seams in the effective runner configuration and both native/prompted structured-output paths')
scenarios: Implementer wires structured-retry + output-token seams into structured_run but expects the transport-attempt bound to also live there, and the one-transport-attempt AC is not actually enforced because the provider transport still reads the run-wide cfg default of 4
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the second repair bullet to state the transport-retry seam is lowered on the effective LLMConfig (e.g. via _effective_config or an equivalent request-local field) so it reaches cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts at the anthropic/bedrock transport builders, while the structured-retry and output-token seams apply in the native/prompted structured-output paths.

findings.checklist_item: Relocate the transport-attempt seam from the structured-output paths to model/transport construction (where stop_after_attempt(cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts) is set), and specify how it flows through get_runner/an injected-or-shared runner without rebuilding a shared transport per call.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:113 `attempts = max(1, int(cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts))` then `stop=stop_after_attempt(attempts)` (line 122) — set once at model/http_client construction
src/rebar/llm/runner.py: model + transport are constructed inside run() from the runner's cfg/resolved, not from req at the structured-output boundary
src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:225,259 — the structured paths carry only output retries (structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES); they never touch the httpx tenacity transport
src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py:182 `get_runner(cfg, override=runner)` — a shared/injected runner's transport is already built from its own cfg
findings.finding: The transport-attempt bound is described as applied in the 'native/prompted structured-output paths,' but the transport retry count is baked into the tenacity AsyncTenacityTransport at model-construction time (_anthropic_model, stop_after_attempt(cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts)), read from LLMConfig and built inside run() BEFORE the structured-output paths execute — so a RunRequest seam applied in those paths cannot lower the transport attempts.
findings.location: Repair plan, bullets 1-2 ('Apply those seams ... in both native/prompted structured-output paths'); AC line 'A failed overlap request makes one transport attempt'
scenarios: Overlap judge request injected with a transport-attempt=1 seam still runs cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts (default 4) transport tries because the seam never reaches transport construction
A shared injected runner reused across calls cannot honor a per-call transport bound without rebuilding the client/transport per request
findings.suggested_fix: State that the per-request transport bound is threaded into _anthropic_model's transport construction (deriving stop_after_attempt from min(cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts, req.transport_attempt_limit)), and describe how an injected/shared runner constructs a per-request client or otherwise honors the lower bound; align the 'transport_attempt' AC accordingly.
